clearedSpotChecks.check: Do the new rules of EIP-8037 change what call(gas(), ...) at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 hands the callee, or let a sub-call fail while the PoolManager call succeeds?
clearedSpotChecks.note: EIP-8037 as fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com on 2026-11-28 says at lines 115-116 that the reservoir passes to the child in full, the 63/64 rule applies to gas_left only, and GAS returns gas_left only. Lines 469 and 505 add that gas_left can rise after a refill, which only matters to code that reads GAS twice. A grep of src/ outside src/test finds no gasleft and only the three call(gas(), ...) sites. Each failure reverts: src/types/Currency.sol:51 and :82 call CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 does the same, and the unlock callback at src/PoolManager.sol:110 is a high-level call that reverts on failure. My own eth_call on ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc) with a parent that forwards gas() to a child returning GAS gave 16,497,333 at 20,000,000 gas, the figure the unit reported. At 30,000,000 the same endpoint gave 29,513,511, which fits the unit's note that the endpoint rotates to Geth backends that skip the cap in eth_call.

clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_config on ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com returned activationTime 1791294816, fork id 0x6c1d9423 and the two builder system contracts, and on ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com returned 1767747671, fork id 0x07c9462e and no next fork, as the unit states. GAS at the first opcode of a 100,000 gas eth_call returned 84,998 on Sepolia and 78,998 on mainnet, which matches the intrinsic cost change from 21,000 to 15,000. Higher state gas only changes whether the caller's own transaction runs out of gas, and an out of gas in any sub-call reverts the whole unlock per the sites above. I did not rerun the pmdiff scripts on Sepolia; I rely on the unit's logs for the call-by-call equality.
